transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I’ve been feeling really down on myself. I keep thinking I’ve let my family down by taking on this mortgage, and then every little mistake I make at work feels like proof that I’m useless… like I deserve whatever happens to me.
How long have you been feeling this way?
It’s been going on for about a year and eight months now. It started after I took on the mortgage for the condo.
Have you noticed any changes in the things you enjoy doing over the past year and eight months?

Yeah… I think so. I used to be more social at work, like joking around with the regulars, and I’d usually text my brother after shifts. Now I mostly just keep a straight face, say what I need to say, and leave it at that. And messages just sit there because I don’t really feel like answering.
Do you still find pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy?

Not really, no. I mean, I used to enjoy joking around with the regulars at work, and I’d usually text my brother after my shifts. Now I mostly just keep a straight face, say what I have to say, and go home. Even messages… I just let them sit there. I don’t really feel the pull to answer.
Have you lost interest in activities that you used to find pleasurable?

Yeah, I have. I don’t really get anything out of the stuff I used to. Like with regulars at work, I used to joke around and enjoy that a bit. Now I mostly just keep my face straight and say only what I need to say. And after shifts, I used to text my brother, but now I just let messages sit there. I don’t really feel like answering.
Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself or ending your life?

I don’t have a plan to hurt myself or anything like that. But… yeah, sometimes when I’m lying awake before an early shift, I think it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up. Like then I wouldn’t have to keep failing at everything.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over the past year and eight months?

Yeah… I think so. My eating’s been pretty up and down. Some weeks I barely touch the staff meal, and then other nights I get home and just eat whatever’s in the kitchen, like I’m trying to settle myself down. So my weight has probably shifted some, but it hasn’t felt steady.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasurable or enjoyable?

Not really. I mean, maybe little things once in a while, but nothing that really pulls me in. I used to enjoy joking with the regulars at work, or texting my brother after a shift. Now I mostly just keep a straight face, say what I need to say, and let messages sit there because I don’t really feel like answering.
Have you had periods of feeling really down before the past year and eight months?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I’ve had rough stretches before, like anyone, but I don’t know if they were the same as this or lasted long enough to call them periods. This last stretch feels more noticeable to me.
Have you had more than one period in your life where you felt this down before the past year and eight months?
I don’t know that I can say more than one, no. I’ve had bad times before, but I can’t really separate them into clear periods like that. This current one is the only one that really stands out to me.
Have you ever felt this down before in your life, prior to the past year and eight months?
I don’t think so. I’ve had times where I was stressed or sad, but not like this, and not where it stuck around in the same way. This is the first time it’s felt this clear to me.
Have you had any other periods in your life where you felt as down as you do now, before the past year and eight months?
No, not really. I’ve felt sad before, but not like this heavy, empty feeling most days. Like I’m just carrying plates and smiling because I’m supposed to, not because I actually feel okay.
Have you had more than one period in your life where you felt as down as you do now?
Not more than one, no. It’s really been this one long stretch. The really depressed and guilty feeling has been around for about a year and a couple months during all of this.
Have you felt as down as you do now before the past year and eight months, more than once?

No, not more than once. Before this past year and eight months, I don’t remember feeling this kind of down. Now it’s most days—just this heavy, empty feeling, like I’m carrying plates and smiling because I have to, not because I actually feel good.
Have you had any periods of feeling significantly better between the times you felt this down?

Not really, no. I mean, there have been days that felt a little lighter, but most of the time through this whole stretch I’ve still had that empty, guilty feeling hanging over me. It’s been there more often than not.
Have you had any periods of feeling significantly down like this before the past year and eight months that lasted for at least two weeks?

No, not before that. This really started about a year and eight months ago, after I took on the condo mortgage. Since then it’s been going on, but I don’t remember having a two-week stretch like this before.
Have you had any periods of feeling significantly down like this before the past year and eight months?
No, not before that. It’s really been this last year and eight months or so, after I took on the condo mortgage, that I’ve felt this way.
Have you had any periods of feeling significantly down like this before the past year and eight months that lasted for at least two weeks?
I don’t think so. I know you asked that already, but before this stretch, I can’t really point to any time where I was down like this for two weeks or more.
Have you had more than one period in your life where you felt as down as you do now?

No, I wouldn’t say more than one. It feels like this same ongoing period. Most days there’s just this heavy, empty feeling in my chest, and I’m kind of going through the motions—working, carrying plates, smiling because I’m supposed to, not because I actually feel good.
Have you had any periods of feeling significantly down like this before the past year and eight months that lasted for at least two weeks and then completely went away?
No, not that I can remember. This has really just been one long stretch for about a year and eight months, since after I took on the condo mortgage. It hasn’t gone away completely in between.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of persistent feelings of worthlessness, guilt, and loss of interest in activities they once enjoyed, along with changes in appetite and sleep, have lasted for more than two years, indicating a persistent depressive disorder. However, given the information provided, the duration and nature of the symptoms more closely align with a single episode of major depressive disorder, which is characterized by one or more major depressive episodes in a person's lifetime, but no manic episodes.
